roleContext.jobDescription: An online marketplace for second-hand furniture is hiring a machine learning engineer into its search team, which ranks about four million listings for every query. The role covers the training pipelines for learning-to-rank models, the offline evaluation harness, A/B test design with the experimentation team and drift monitoring of the ranking features. Over time the engineer is expected to set technical direction for the ranking roadmap and to present the trade-offs between relevance, latency and seller fairness to product leadership in the quarterly planning review.

requirements.text: Builds training pipelines for learning-to-rank models in Python.
Maintains an offline evaluation harness with ranking metrics such as NDCG.
Designs and analyses online A/B tests of ranking changes with the experimentation team.
Sets technical direction for the ranking roadmap and presents trade-offs to product leadership.
Monitors feature drift in the ranking feature store.

candidate.originalCvMarkdown:
# Curriculum vitae

Target role: Machine Learning Engineer, Search Ranking

## Experience

- Machine learning engineer at Lumenwick (e-commerce search software), February 2022 to present, building the Python training pipeline for the gradient-boosted learning-to-rank model used by the retail search product.
- Maintained the offline evaluation harness, computing NDCG@10 and mean reciprocal rank on a frozen query set for every candidate model before it could be proposed for testing.
- Wrote the analysis plans for three A/B tests of ranking changes with the experimentation team, specifying the primary metric, sample size and stopping rule in advance.
- Added drift checks on the 40 most-used ranking features, alerting when the population stability index went above 0.2 for two consecutive days.
- Presented the evaluation results for each model candidate at the fortnightly ranking review attended by the search engineers and the search product manager.

## Work samples

- Work sample: an offline evaluation report comparing two ranking model candidates on the frozen query set, with NDCG@10, MRR, a breakdown by query segment and a note on how the queries were sampled.
